findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a new story has two unordered parts whose production scopes overlap.
`forge read` calls `plan_scope.check`, whose refusal still says only that the tasks can change the same file and lists their scopes (`src/forge/plan_scope.py:23-27`). For `src/api/**` and `src/**/routes/*`, it neither identifies `src/api/` as the shared path nor says this is a scope overlap. The owner-approved Done-when requires: "A part whose Scope shares only a test folder with another open part starts without waiting, and a refusal caused by a real scope overlap names the shared path and says it is a scope overlap."

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - the pull request runs its related tests.
The added sentence changes the first line of a `stack = "off"` overlap refusal. `tests/test_fullcap_start.py:55-57` and `:75-77` still compare that line exactly with the old text, so its overlap case fails when `Scope overlap: app.py.` is appended. The full suite also retains the old exact refusal in `tests/test_task.py:111-114` and `:142-148`. Update those expectations while retaining their checks of the refusal and next step.
findings.title: Gate: Existing task-start tests reject the new refusal text

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - one open part has `tests/` in Scope and another needs to change `tests/test_routes.py`.
The new exception lets both parts start, but `src/forge/worker.py:63-64` still tells the second worker to leave any file owned by another open task's Scope, which includes that test file. The planning instructions in `src/forge/templates/story.md:64-65`, `src/forge/templates/cold-read.md:156-160`, and `docs/guide.md:290-294` also still describe every shared prefix as requiring a refusal or dependency. Workers and readers therefore receive instructions that contradict the new rule and can leave the intended parallel work incomplete.
findings.title: Functional: Align planning and worker guidance with shared test folders

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a repo adopted on an earlier Forge release upgrades and starts story parts.
The supposed earlier-adopted case copies the old fixture and then replaces its entire `forge.toml` with a version-only file; it never runs the upgrade or syncs the old guides. It therefore cannot establish that the new behavior reaches a client with its existing settings and updated guidance. The real-overlap refusal test at `tests/test_scope_overlap_explains_waits.py:42-44` also runs only on the fresh fixture. The repository's review rule requires an earlier-adopted case for each changed rule.
findings.title: Gate: Prove both overlap rules for an upgraded client

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a new story has two parts whose only shared Scope is a test folder and must pass `forge read` before approval.
The new admission test creates already-approved stories through `story()` at `tests/test_scope_overlap_explains_waits.py:34` and `:37`, so it never exercises `plan_scope.check`. The existing plan-check cases in `tests/test_splitreview_plan.py:19-30` cover production paths but no test-folder exception. Restoring the old plan overlap rule would leave the new tests passing while refusing such a plan before its parts can start. Add a command-level plan-check case for the exception.
findings.title: Gate: Exercise shared test folders through the plan check

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
The new cases cover a folder Scope against a file Scope, with no explicit dependency. They would still pass if an implementation exempted only folder entries, leaving two parts naming the same test file waiting, or skipped an explicit `After` prerequisite whenever test paths overlap. Those are separate cases of the coordinator's recorded ruling.
Adds work: exercise exact-file scopes and an explicit prerequisite; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4

why: A folder in Scope, such as a test folder, overlaps every part that touches any file under it, so parts across stories wait on each other, and the refusal says only that the part builds on another part without naming the shared path or saying it is a scope overlap.
